solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country, for example, bordered by roads from the east

indicators.note: bordered by says the roads piece sits on either side of the example abbreviation
from the east, in an across clue, says the roads word is read right to left

parts.note: roads are lanes
EG is the abbreviation for for example (exempli gratia)

explanation.surface: A geography note describing some nation hemmed in by highways on its eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns LANES into SENAL, and EG goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a West African nation, so it is an instance of a country.

clue.text: Down-at-heel bloke gets right into scrape

indicators.note: into says the right abbreviation goes inside the scrape word

parts.note: to scuff is to scrape

explanation.surface: A shabby man getting himself into a spot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; 'scrape' sounds like trouble but is SCUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is informal British for a scruffy, untidy person.

clue.text: Foreign currency invested in new name for nerve cell

indicators.note: invested in says the currency is placed between the two abbreviations

parts.note: the euro is a foreign currency to a British solver

explanation.surface: Overseas money is put into a new name for some nerve tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is the basic cell of the nervous system that carries signals.

clue.text: You once invested in divine European accommodation for travellers

indicators.note: invested in says the old pronoun is placed inside the divine word

parts.note: to divine is to guess
thou is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: An old form of address placed in a holy European lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective (holy); it is the verb meaning to guess.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesthouse is a small private hotel offering lodging for visitors.

clue.text: Fail, catching union leader's bug

indicators.note: catching says the fail word holds the leader inside it

parts.note: to lose is to fail

indicators.note: leader's means the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A failure to catch the leader of a trade union who has a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small parasitic insect, loosely called a bug.

clue.text: Deer from estate, say — one about to lose protection

parts.note: an estate is a kind of car, the British name for a station wagon
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to lose protection says the word about sheds its outer letters, its protective shell

explanation.surface: A sighting of deer on a country estate, with one animal shedding its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon. 'to lose protection' strips the outer A and T from ABOUT, leaving BOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a species of deer.

clue.text: Own up and arrive free of drugs

parts.note: to arrive is to come
clean in slang means no longer using drugs

explanation.surface: An addict confesses and turns up sober.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing, telling the truth about something.

clue.text: Not often experienced, but runs a race, disheartened

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: disheartened says race loses its middle letters, its heart

explanation.surface: A runner who seldom competes and loses heart during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips the middle AC from RACE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon, seldom met with.

clue.text: Black reptile reported in snowstorm

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: reported says the reptile word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile

explanation.surface: A dark reptile is sighted in a heavy snowfall.
explanation.walkthrough: LIZZARD, the second half of the answer, sounds like LIZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong wind.

clue.text: Reporting to fix support

parts.note: someone reporting to a manager works under them
to fix something in place is to pin it

explanation.surface: Advice on reporting to someone to fix a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporting' looks like journalism; with 'to' it means being answerable to, i.e. under.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to support from beneath, as a building's foundations.

clue.text: Disturb game bird, blowing head off!

indicators.note: blowing head off says the bird loses its first letter

parts.note: the grouse is a game bird shot for sport

explanation.surface: A shooting party startles a game bird and blasts its head off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to wake or stir them, a synonym of disturb.

clue.text: Single admirer spoilt by a Parisian

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: spoilt says the letters of admirer are ruined and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lonely heart whose admirer is ruined by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like the numeric sense, one; it is the marital status. The French indefinite article stands for 'a Parisian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Single, as a marital status, means not wed to anyone.

clue.text: Where ministers face magistrates?

parts.note: the face of something is its front
magistrates collectively are the bench

explanation.surface: A question about where government ministers go to confront the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British House of Commons, government ministers sit on the front row facing the opposition; 'the bench' is the collective term for magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior ministers in Parliament sit on the foremost seats, so this seating is where they are.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying unknown ruler

indicators.note: carrying says the vehicle holds the unknown inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A carriage transporting a mystery monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A czar (tsar) was the emperor of Russia, so a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Gathered together and confined following poor beggar that had been executed

indicators.note: following says the confined word comes after the jumbled letters
poor says the remaining letters are in a bad, jumbled state
executed means beheaded, so the word beggar loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
gated means confined to school or home as a punishment

explanation.surface: A poor beggar who had been put to death is locked up and rounded up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' beheads BEGGAR to EGGAR, which 'poor' rearranges into AGGRE. Gated is British slang for grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregated means collected or combined into a single mass or total.

clue.text: A grin spreads after compliment for flavouring

indicators.note: after says the rearranged grin follows the compliment

parts.note: a bouquet is a compliment or tribute

indicators.note: spreads says the letters of a grin are stretched into a new order

explanation.surface: A smile widens after someone receives praise for their seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet garni is a bundle of herbs used to season soups and stews.

clue.text: 'Too quaint' possibly identifies this

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of too quaint might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A remark that a phrase in inverted commas is a bit old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TOO QUAINT is the answer, and the inverted commas around those words mark them as just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Words placed in inverted commas are a quoted extract, which is what the clue shows.

clue.text: Cut of meat for Cliff in post?

indicators.note: in says the cliff word goes inside the post word

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a crag is a cliff

explanation.surface: A man named Cliff working at the post office, offered as a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' looks like a man's name; it is a crag. Scrag end is the bony neck of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is the inferior neck portion of mutton or lamb, a cheap butchery joint.

clue.text: Decorator — till actually holding a dish from Spain

indicators.note: holding says the phrase before it contains the answer in its letters

explanation.surface: A painter at the shop till is actually carrying a Spanish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish tortilla is a potato omelette, not the Mexican flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain a tortilla is a thick egg and potato omelette, a national dish.

clue.text: Symbol representing a Christian nation or race

parts.note: the cross is the emblem of Christianity
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Discussion of what emblem stands for a Christian state or people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like it continues 'nation' (a people); it is the definition, a running race.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-country is a running race over open fields and rough terrain rather than a track.

clue.text: Decoration for which I must be put in last

indicators.note: must be put in says the letter goes inside the word for last

parts.note: the last item in a series is the final one

explanation.surface: A decoration for which the speaker must take last place.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is an ornament topping a spire, gable or post.

clue.text: Newspaper chief called it ordinary, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss dismissed something as merely ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor is the person in charge of a newspaper's content.

clue.text: Pretentious soirée starting late

indicators.note: starting late says the first letter is missing, as if the word turned up after its start

parts.note: a soirée is an evening party

explanation.surface: An affected evening gathering that gets going behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone affectedly showing off artistic taste, hence pretentious.

clue.text: Silly bidding war for rail, for example

indicators.note: silly says the letters of bidding war are scrambled foolishly

explanation.surface: A foolish auction contest over railway stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' suggests a railway or banister; here it is a marsh bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail is a marsh bird that wades in shallow water, an example of the class.

clue.text: Acquired following in bar

indicators.note: following says the acquired word comes after in

parts.note: acquired means got

explanation.surface: Something obtained after going into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is a bar of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block or bar of cast metal, especially gold.

clue.text: Log salmon regularly appearing in city

indicators.note: regularly appearing says every second letter of log salmon is taken

explanation.surface: A record of salmon seen at intervals in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Joining forces, being inclined to follow nurse

indicators.note: to follow says the inclined word comes after the nurse

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
a ship listing is leaning or inclined

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to sign up behind a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: EN stands for Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting means signing up to the armed forces, i.e. joining them.

clue.text: An unexpected development in dance

definitions.meaning: a sudden change in a plot or story

explanation.definitionFit: A plot surprise and a 1960s gyrating dance craze share this name.

clue.text: Shanghai's duck-eating breather of fire

indicators.note: eating says the fire-breather swallows the duck

parts.note: a dragon breathes fire
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast from a Chinese city devours a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanghai' looks like the Chinese city; it is the verb, to force someone into service. A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai and to dragoon both mean to coerce someone into doing something.

clue.text: Time and pounds invested in more unusual child

indicators.note: invested in says the pounds are placed inside the unusual word

parts.note: odder means more unusual
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Time and money spent on a rather strange youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a very young child just learning to walk.
